why: The statement asks for an estimate of the constant c = lim M(n)/n, and nothing in the record determines it, so every substantive event is a bound on one side. The 2025-26 step functions (AlphaEvolve, TTT-Discover, Aster, SimpleTES, arena entries, MILO) lower the upper bound; Kim-Pilanci and the Price/emerardd/ruturajr-raval certificates raise the lower bound. TTT-Discover is marked checkable because its explicit, released step function was checked numerically by a named reviewer (Torlo). That check covers the arithmetic, which is the whole of the claim once the standard reduction is accepted. Other step functions were not located, so they stay unreviewed. The machine-checked lower-bound certificates are large interval-arithmetic computations, too big to count as simple checks, so they are unreviewed. AI roles: AlphaEvolve, TTT-Discover, Aster, SimpleTES and MILO are credited as the producers of the constructions, so generated. Kim-Pilanci is assisted: a human-designed convex program plus constraints the agent found. Price's certificate is generated on the poster's own words, though no model is named in the repo. The arena entries have no systems recorded, so none. The Georgiev-Tao paper restates an earlier bound, so scope none. The GCL small-n enumeration is instances.
doubts: The AI credit for Price's 0.38055470 rests only on a forum post ('GPT Pro'); if that is wrong, the lower-bound AI role would drop. Together AI's 'internal agents' and CodexProLong were plausibly AI, but no system was recorded, so they are scored none. All quotes came through a summarising fetch tool.
